patches.new_string:
Of those three remaining post-hoc rescues, the LaCoste-Romberg-spring sensitivity-floor defense (the assertion that the 1999 and 2009 SG/spring networks — seven of whose eight 2009 instruments were spring gravimeters — were too noisy to register a κ-coupled few-µGal pulse, so the null is an absence of detection rather than evidence of absence) is dissected at WIN-014’s detail prose as a symmetric tu quoque: any spring-class distrust strict enough to excuse the 2009 eight-instrument null from bounding a 3–9 µGal prediction annihilates the single LaCoste-Romberg model D spring (D-122, stated precision 2–3 µGal, residual band ±3–4 µGal per Wang et al. 2000) that anchors κ’s 6.5 µGal denominator first — and √8 ≈ 2.8× network stacking of the eight 2009 spring records puts the spring-only network floor at ∼1.1–1.4 µGal, 2–8× below the prediction, so the bound holds even without an SG. Consistent application of the sensitivity defense therefore deletes κ rather than rescuing WIN-014; the dome cannot wield it without forfeiting the constant the vise depends on. (Full retraction chain — Yang & Wang 2002, Van Flandern & Yang 2003, and the 2013 CJG weather attribution by the original Mohe authors — is at WIN-014.detail_evidence.)

The Chebychev-low-pass argument warrants its own dissection because methodologically it is the most plausible-sounding — and, on the published record, the most fully refuted.
